description: Audit logs of version 1 and logs that mix versions 0 and 1, with the expected result of the verification, SPEC-v0.md sections 9.4 and 14. Besides valid and broken_at, a case states the three findings of section 9.4: integrity_broken_at, conformance_broken_at and unknown_version_at, each absent if there is none. Entries of the unknown version 2 stand for any version a verifier does not know. Checkpoints are signed with the test key test-ed25519 of conformance/keys/test-keys.private.json.

logs.why: every new event of version 1, in a log of version 1
a log that continues in version 1 after entries of version 0 (SPEC-v0 section 14, mixed data)

a checkpoint of version 1 at the change of version anchors the part of version 0, and a checkpoint in version 1 signs the payload type audit-checkpoint/v0; the rollout asks a writer for a checkpoint of version 0 as the last entry before the first of version 1, which a verifier does not check (SPEC-v0 section 14)
an entry of version 0 after an entry of version 1 breaks condition 1
an event of version 1 under the type of version 0
an entry of a version this verifier does not know: the log is not damaged; from there on its content is not checked (SPEC-v0 section 9.4)
an entry changed before an entry of an unknown version: the chain is still checked, and the change breaks it
a break of the chain after an entry of an unknown version is still found
an unknown version in the first entry
an entry of version 1 after one of an unknown newer version: an older version after a newer one breaks condition 1, known or not (SPEC-v0 section 14)

a rewritten history whose signed checkpoint was given an unknown version, so that it would not be checked: a checkpoint is checked whatever its version, and the rewrite breaks the integrity (SPEC-v0 sections 9.4 and 9.5)
a deleted beginning covered by a log.truncated entry of an unknown version: the log is not damaged
credentials of one agent without the agent
credentials of all agents with an agent
an unexpected certificate without its names
an acknowledgement names the digest and nothing else (SPEC-v0 section 11.7 item 7)
a public origin with the default port written out: a pattern allows it, the rule of SPEC-v0 section 11.7 item 1 does not
a public origin with a path
a member of the relay object that another event uses
new pins without an active pin
the binding of an agent on a decision
a status of Certificate Transparency monitoring that equals the previous one
a version with a leading zero names no audit version
a home ID that is not 26 characters of base32
credentials withdrawn with an emergency stop are those of every agent
a pairing is chosen by a human
credentials a human withdrew name that human
the names and the issuer of a certificate come from whoever obtained it: control characters and a direction mark are recorded unchanged, and the entry is valid (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)

a request for four resources that the approver rejected: the entries that lead to ask carry the same approval object, and every entry, the allow and the deny that audit mode does not enforce included, records the denial of the whole request (SPEC-v0 sections 4.4 and 9.1)

a request for three resources one of which a rule denies: nothing is executed, and the deny that audit mode does not enforce is recorded as denied by the mandate because the request carries a group (SPEC-v0 sections 4.4 and 9.1)
a deny that audit mode does not enforce, recorded as denied by the mandate without a group: only the denial of a whole request for several resources may be recorded so (SPEC-v0 sections 4.6 and 9.1)
a confirmation that had expired when the action would have been executed: not executed, denied by the approval with the approval that was given (SPEC-v0 section 11.1 item 5)

a request for a renamed resource before a human resolved the rename: one entry for the current and one for the former identifier, with the same group; the stricter decides and nothing is executed (SPEC-v0 section 11.4)
approval requests that are not made: no common approver of the resources, and a repeated call tied to the waiting request; no approval object, the cause in error (SPEC-v0 section 11.1 items 7 and 12)
a request for three resources that the common approver confirmed: the entries that lead to ask carry the same approval object, and every entry records the execution (SPEC-v0 section 4.4)
a request for two resources one of which a rule denies: nobody is asked, and the entry that would lead to ask is denied by the mandate without an approval object (SPEC-v0 section 4.4)
a deny that audit mode does not enforce, in a request with a group, denied by the rate limit: the rate limit comes before any evaluation (SPEC-v0 sections 9.1 and 11.2)
a deny that audit mode does not enforce, recorded as denied by the approval without a group (SPEC-v0 sections 4.6 and 9.1)

two entries of version 1 with the same id: a writer gives every entry a new UUIDv7, but a repeat is no finding of the verifier, since nothing refers to an entry by its id and whoever can write the log can recompute the chain anyway (SPEC-v0 sections 9.1 and 9.4)

checkpoints of version 1 whose log_id is a UUID of version 1: from audit/v1 on, a log_id is a UUID of version 4 or 7 (SPEC-v0 section 9.5), so the first breaks condition 1; without keys the signatures are not checked (SPEC-v0 sections 9.4 and 9.5)
an entry of version 1 with the id of an earlier entry of version 0: a repeated id is no finding of the verifier, whatever the versions (SPEC-v0 section 9.4)

mandate.rejected of version 1, each with received, the SHA-256 of the bytes as they arrived: a signed mandate whose signature does not verify (with digest, which differs from received), bytes that are not JSON (only cause and received) and a JSON object with a duplicate key, which has no canonical form and so no digest (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
mandate.rejected of version 1 without received: required in version 1, so the entry breaks condition 1 (SPEC-v0 sections 9.1 and 9.4)
mandate.proposed with received: only mandate.rejected has it (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
received with upper-case hexadecimal digits: a digest is written in lower case (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
received with another algorithm (sha512): received is SHA-256 in this version (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
received with 63 hexadecimal digits instead of 64 (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
a log that switches from version 0 to version 1: the mandate.rejected entries of version 0 have no received and stay valid, the one of version 1 has it (SPEC-v0 sections 9.1 and 14)

a request for two resources denied as a whole: the entry of the resource that a deny rule and an ask rule both match (enforced false, confirm true) is denied by the mandate without an approval object, because nobody was asked (SPEC-v0 sections 4.4 and 9.1)
the same entry outside a request for several resources: with confirm true, denied_by mandate needs an approval object (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
duration_ms of 2^53: a number that is not an integer of a magnitude below 2^53 has no digest, so the entry takes no part in the chain (SPEC-v0 section 9.4)
duration_ms of 120.5: a number that is not an integer has no digest, so the entry takes no part in the chain (SPEC-v0 section 9.4)

a noncharacter in an entry of version 1: the correction of section 14 applies only to audit/v0, so the entry breaks condition 1; it keeps its digest and the chain is intact (SPEC-v0 sections 9.4 and 14)
a checkpoint without log_id, verified without keys: it cannot be checked and breaks condition 4, an integrity finding, besides the schema (SPEC-v0 sections 9.4 and 9.5)
a checkpoint without signature, verified without keys: it cannot be checked and breaks condition 4, an integrity finding, besides the schema (SPEC-v0 sections 9.4 and 9.5)
exchange format: a line of 70 000 bytes, longer than an entry may be, does not end the reading; the entry of an unknown version after it is still reported (SPEC-v0 section 9.4)

values of version 1 for removed settings, the key agents are shown, a trusted proxy, a reused refresh token, an acknowledgement by public key, and the events and values of a gateway paired with a relay (SPEC-v0 sections 9.1 and 9.2, RELAY-v0)
the time zone cannot be removed: config.changed for timezone needs a value (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
config.changed with neither value nor previous_value (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
a reused refresh token ends the tokens of one agent, never of all (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
cert.acknowledged names a certificate by its digest or by its public key, not by both (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
replaced is no cause of relay.unpaired: a gateway cannot tell a replacement from another end of its installation (SPEC-v0 section 9.2, RELAY-v0 section 5.2)
relay.monitoring_status knows only ok and unavailable (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.status_changed knows only the statuses of an installation (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.pin_mismatch names only the operator (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.replacement_pending names the end of the waiting time (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)

the writer kept no cadence of checkpoints: an entry was appended within 24 hours of the last checkpoint, and the next entry, recorded more than 24 hours after it, is not a checkpoint; the log is valid, and checkpoint_gap_at names that entry (SPEC-v0 section 9.5)
no entry within 24 hours of the last checkpoint, then one entry and a checkpoint directly after it: no gap (SPEC-v0 section 9.5)
a checkpoint that comes more than 24 hours after the previous one although an entry was appended in between is itself the gap (SPEC-v0 section 9.5)

in a request for several resources, an entry with confirm true and denied_by mandate may lack an approval object, but one it has is approved or cancelled with cause revoked, as outside a group (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
an IPv6 address in upper case: a trusted proxy is written in its canonical text form (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
a prefix with host bits set: a trusted proxy is written in its canonical text form (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
an IPv6 address that is not compressed as RFC 5952 writes it: a trusted proxy is written in its canonical text form (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
an IPv4 address with a leading zero: a trusted proxy is written in its canonical text form (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)
trusted proxies in their canonical text form: an IPv4 prefix, an IPv6 prefix, and an IPv6 address removed (SPEC-v0 section 9.1)

what a gateway paired with a relay refuses: a pairing response that fails a check, a set of pins it ignores for each reason, and metadata whose pins share none with the stored ones (SPEC-v0 section 9.2, RELAY-v0)
relay.pairing_refused names the check that failed (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.pairing_refused knows only the checks name and certificate (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.monitoring_status knows only the checks caa and installation (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.pins_ignored knows only the reasons rules, connection_pin, storage and limit (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
relay.metadata_pins_unknown names only the operator (SPEC-v0 section 9.2)
